newsitem.title: FRANCE: FOCUS - French banks cut base lending rates.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS - French banks cut base lending rates.

text.p: France's major commercial banks said on Monday they were reducing their base lending rates to keep up with a recent drop in French market rates.

Most of France's big mainstream banks including Societe Generale Banque Nationale de Paris, Credit Lyonnais and Credit Commercial de France (CCF) along with regional banking group CIC said they were reducing their base rates to 6.30 percent from 6.55 percent, effective December 18.
"Given the change in market rates, BNP announces the reduction in its base lending rate," the bank said in a brief statement, virtually identical to other banks' announcements.
Economists, who acknowledged the banks' stated reasoning, said their move was also a reflection of renewed confidence that French official interest rates would continue to fall.
"The banks are late," said Valerie Plagnol, economist with CCF. "But this is clearly a sign of confidence linked to the stability pact and the outlook for rates."
She was referring to an agreement by European Union (EU) countries on a budget discipline pact, known as the "stability pact", reached at the weekend during an EU summit in Dublin.
The pact is meant to ensure that EU countries participating in a single currency do not run excessive deficits.
Many French economists said they expect the Bank of France to lower its key intervention rate, which sets the floor on money market rates, very soon.
Some said the first easing could come later this week, while others predicted the central bank would wait until early next year.
The banks last cut their base rates at which they lend to their best customers on September 20. Monday's easing was the fourth time this year the banks had cut the rates.
The centre-right government has been urging commercial banks to pass on interest rate cuts by the Bank of France.
The Bank left its intervention rate unchanged at 3.20 percent earlier on Monday at its regular money market tender.
